content.user_title: Analyze Startup Markets and Financial Models
content.value_statement: Early-stage teams need defensible market, financial, and strategy analysis for funding and planning. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to build cited startup analyses, models, and recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Guides TAM, SAM, and SOM analysis using bottom-up, top-down, and value theory methods.
Builds revenue, cost, runway, and scenario assumptions for three to five year models.
Assesses unit economics such as CAC, LTV, payback period, burn multiple, and magic number.
Structures competitive landscape, positioning, and differentiation analysis.
Plans early-stage hiring, compensation, equity, and organization design by stage.
Produces investor-ready analysis sections with assumptions, benchmarks, sources, and next steps.
limitations: It does not replace legal, tax, accounting, or investment advice.
Current market data requires web search and source validation.
Financial outputs depend on the quality of user assumptions and inputs.
Compensation benchmarks are US-focused and may not fit every region.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Fundraising Case
use_cases.description: Build market sizing, financial assumptions, and milestone plans before investor outreach.

use_cases.title: Review an Investment Opportunity
use_cases.description: Compare market size, traction signals, unit economics, and competitive position before deeper diligence.

use_cases.title: Plan an Operating Cycle
use_cases.description: Turn strategy questions into hiring, runway, pricing, and KPI plans for the next operating cycle.
use_cases.target_user: Startup operator or chief of staff

prompt_templates.title: Size My Market
prompt_templates.prompt: I am building [product] for [customer] in [geography]. Estimate TAM, SAM, and SOM using available data, show assumptions, and list sources.

prompt_templates.title: Check Unit Economics
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these inputs: [price], [gross margin], [CAC], [retention], [sales cycle], and [payback target]. Assess LTV, CAC payback, and investment readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Fundraising Milestones
prompt_templates.prompt: I am raising [round] with [current traction], [runway], and [team]. Build a milestone plan, funding need, and investor evidence checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Build Scenario Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Create conservative, base, and upside scenarios for [business model]. Include revenue drivers, hiring plan, cash runway, risks, and board-level recommendations.

output_examples.input: Founder asks for TAM, SAM, and SOM for a construction project management SaaS product.
output: Defines buyer segments, geography, and pricing assumptions.
Shows bottom-up and top-down market estimates with source notes.
Explains which estimate is most defensible for a seed pitch.

output_examples.input: Seed-stage SaaS team shares MRR, CAC, churn, gross margin, and planned hiring.
output: Calculates LTV, CAC payback, burn multiple, and runway.
Flags weak assumptions and missing retention data.
Recommends conservative, base, and upside operating scenarios.

output_examples.input: Operator compares sales-led and product-led go-to-market options.
output: Maps customer segments, sales cycle, pricing, and support burden.
Compares expected growth rate, capital need, and operational risk.
Recommends the path with measurable validation milestones.

best_practices: Provide stage, geography, customer segment, revenue model, and known traction before asking for analysis.
Ask for assumptions, source dates, and sensitivity ranges with every estimate.
Review outputs with finance, legal, or domain experts before fundraising or investment decisions.
anti_patterns: Treating market-size estimates as facts without source validation.
Asking for a full strategy without sharing stage, target customer, or constraints.
Using optimistic scenarios as the only plan for hiring, runway, or fundraising.

faq.question: Does this skill create financial spreadsheets?
faq.answer: It can outline model structure, assumptions, formulas, and scenario logic. Spreadsheet generation depends on the host tool and available file access.

faq.question: Can it use current market data?
faq.answer: Yes, when web search is available. It should cite source dates and note data quality limits.

faq.question: Is it suitable for later-stage companies?
faq.answer: It is optimized for pre-seed through Series A. Later-stage work may need deeper finance and operating detail.

faq.question: Does it give investment advice?
faq.answer: No. It supports analysis and planning, but users should consult qualified advisors before investment decisions.

faq.question: Which startup models does it support?
faq.answer: It covers SaaS, marketplaces, consumer products, B2B, fintech, and other early-stage models.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is declared for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.
